correctness.rationale: On the exact positive-parameter resonance, the two multipliers are 1−e and 1+ke; positive iterates require −1/k<e<1. Weighted AM–GM yields (1−e)^k(1+ke)<1 for every e≠0, proving strict Lyapunov descent. Positivity of multipliers forces d/k<H<m and boundedness. Nonzero limiting product yields compact interior, e_n→0, a finite at-most-two-point limit set from unimodality of V along E, vanishing increments and thus convergence to a single equilibrium. Zero limiting product implies min(x_n,y_n)→0. The transverse Jacobian spectrum is exact; the normally contracting interval is open and nonempty. Executed SymPy checker confirms algebraic identities and a rational witness, not infinite-time claims.

value.rationale: This parameter resonance is a naturally motivated loss of uniqueness of positive equilibria in a published discrete predator–prey model. The result gives a complete all-period positive-recurrence obstruction and a global positive-orbit convergence dichotomy despite a fixed continuum, together with a sharp normally contracting subsegment and a transverse −1 boundary without emergent positive two-cycles. These are qualitatively structural facts, not numerical period enumeration, textbook eigenvalue tests, or arbitrary parameter slices.
